parents.course: Writing about Literature, Text, and Culture

ns2:section.sectionText: What happens once the apocalypse is over? Sure, in your average post-apocalyptic narrative, cities are burned, populations are infected, food supplies are disrupted . . . but so much remains! This course will begin at the end, with texts such as: The Road, Oryx and Crake, The Sheep Look Up, The Country of Last Things, The Mandibles: A Family, 2029-2047, Wastelands: Stories of the Apocalypse, and plenty of multi-media, and interdisciplinary non-fiction. We’ll ask why are we so obsessed with the end of the world; but we'll also ask why and how we choose to rebuild. Our course fulfills the Advanced Composition requirement, so there will be plenty of writing . . . but the topics and format will be largely up to you--take the traditional paper route, or opt into so many other styles and formats!
